## Context / Problem

`docs/api-stability.md:24,41-46` defines underscore-prefixed modules/functions as private, while ADR 0083 already requires one canonical binding for reconciler moves. Contrary decisions remain: ADR 0016 retains `run_security_detectors`, ADR 0092 retains reconcile compatibility, and past split documentation retained private shims to avoid consumer migration.

## Approach

Complete the prescribed ADR lifecycle. In RESEARCH, catalog the cited contrary decisions and write a numbered critique covering public-versus-private boundaries, dynamic/monkeypatch consumers, persisted/wire exceptions, and enforcement. Record maintainer resolution for every critique item. Then DRAFT, HOLD for review, and MERGE an ADR that mandates one canonical private binding and atomic consumer migration.

## Scope

- new ADR allocated through `docs/adr/.numbers`
- `docs/api-stability.md` and architecture/reuse guidance
- enforcement/review guidance or a mechanical guard identified by the ADR

## Testing

Add a policy/documentation check or deterministic enforcement test specified by the ADR; verify existing public facade, wire-schema, and persisted-event contract tests remain unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] RESEARCH contains a numbered critique of ADR 0016, ADR 0083, ADR 0092, and prior split-shim guidance; each item has a recorded maintainer resolution.
- [x] The merged ADR defines one canonical binding after private moves and atomic source/test/string/dynamic/monkeypatch migration.
- [x] The ADR distinguishes valid public facades, MCP wire schemas, event readers, and persisted-data migrations from internal-only shims.
- [x] The ADR requires a durable review or mechanical recurrence-prevention mechanism and names its evidence.
- [x] The policy check/enforcement evidence passes without breaking the preserved public/wire/event contracts.
